newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian plane lost on way from Port Harcourt.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian plane lost on way from Port Harcourt.

text.p: A passenger plane with 141 people on board is missing on a flight from the southeast Nigerian oil city of Port Harcourt. Airport sources said it was presumed to have crashed.
Several foreigners were on board, possibly oil company executives, aviation sources said.

Aviation Development Company, a private Nigerian airline, said its Boeing 727 was flying from Port Harcourt to Lagos with 132 passengers and nine crew members when it lost contact with the control tower.
Flight ADC086's last contact with the control tower in Lagos was at 5 p.m. (1600 GMT), it said. "A search and rescue operation is going on."
A company spokesman told Reuters "We still have no further information. We are expecting the manifest from Port Harcourt."
Western diplomats said they had unconfirmed information that the plane crashed around a small town called Shagamu about 100 km (60 miles) from Lagos.
But the ADC spokesman said "For now nobody knows what has happened to the plane. Our people are still out and about searching."
Economic troubles have weakened Nigeria's infrastructure in recent years and there has been a spate of air disasters.
ADC is 100 percent owned by Nigerian shareholders. It operates domestic services and flies to some West African countries. One of its planes crashed in Liberia last year.
In January a presidential jet crashed in the north killing the son of military ruler General Sani Abacha. Another crash in Jos, central Nigeria, killed a state military governor.
